**Week‑Long Dinner Plan for Extra Satiety**  
*Designed for someone who skips lunch and eats only breakfast and dinner. Each dinner emphasizes protein + fiber, slow‑digesting carbs, and healthy fats to keep you full through the evening and overnight.*

| Day | Main Dish (≈ 350‑500 kcal) | Filling Sides (≈ 150‑250 kcal) | Why It Works |
|-----|----------------------------|--------------------------------|--------------|
| **Monday** | **Grilled salmon** (150 g) with lemon‑herb rub | Quinoa tabbouleh (½ cup cooked quinoa, chopped cucumber, tomato, parsley, olive‑oil dressing) + roasted broccoli (1 cup) | Salmon supplies 25‑30 g high‑quality protein; quinoa adds plant protein and fiber; olive oil brings satiety‑boosting fat [[summaries/session-32_2024-12-16]]. |
| **Tuesday** | **Turkey & black‑bean chili** (1 ½ cups) – ground turkey, black beans, diced tomatoes, bell pepper, cumin | Side of brown‑rice (½ cup) and a small avocado slice | Turkey and beans give 30 g protein + soluble fiber; brown rice supplies slow carbs; avocado adds healthy monounsaturated fat for prolonged fullness. |
| **Wednesday** | **Stir‑fried tofu** (200 g) with mixed veg (snap peas, carrots, bok choy) in sesame‑ginger sauce | Whole‑grain soba noodles (¾ cup) + a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds | Tofu delivers plant protein; veg provide fiber; soba noodles contribute complex carbs; sesame seeds add fat and crunch. |
| **Thursday** | **Baked chicken thigh** (2 small thighs) with rosemary‑garlic | Sweet‑potato mash (½ cup) + sautéed kale with garlic (1 cup) | Chicken thighs are a modestly fattier protein source, helping satiety; sweet potato gives resistant starch; kale adds bulk and fiber. |
| **Friday** | **Lentil‑spinach curry** (1 ½ cups) cooked with coconut milk, garam masala | Cauliflower “rice” (1 cup) + a dollop of Greek yogurt | Lentils supply 18 g protein + soluble fiber; coconut milk adds medium‑chain fats; yogurt adds extra protein and a cooling element. |
| **Saturday** | **Grass‑fed beef stir‑fry** (150 g strips) with bell peppers, onions, mushrooms | Farro pilaf (½ cup cooked) + side salad (mixed greens, olives, feta, olive‑oil vinaigrette) | Beef delivers dense protein + iron; farro contributes chewiness and fiber; olives/feta contribute fat for long‑lasting fullness. |
| **Sunday** | **Baked cod** (180 g) with pesto sauce | Barley risotto (½ cup) with peas + roasted Brussels sprouts (1 cup) | Cod is a lean protein; pesto adds pine nuts (fat) and basil (flavor); barley is high in β‑glucan fiber, slowing digestion. |

### How These Dinners Meet the “Extra Filling” Goal
1. **Protein ≥ 30 g per meal** – the primary driver of satiety [[summaries/session-32_2024-12-16]].
2. **Fiber‑rich vegetables and whole grains** – slow nutrient absorption, keeping hunger at bay for 4‑6 hours.
3. **Healthy fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, coconut milk, cheese)** – lengthen gastric emptying and enhance feeling of fullness.
4. **Balanced calorie range** – larger than a typical light dinner but still within a moderate total (≈ 500‑750 kcal) so you won’t feel overly heavy before bedtime.
5. **Variety of textures and flavors** – reduces “meal fatigue” and makes sticking to the plan easier.

Feel free to swap side portions up or down depending on your personal energy needs; the guide gives a solid baseline for a filling dinner that compensates for the missing midday meal.
